title: A Promise Made Under Pressure
script: Fikri: [worried] Hasan, I told the community center I could design all twelve posters by Friday.
Hasan: That is a large task. How many have you finished?
Fikri: [panicked] Only two. My work deadline also moved forward, and I am starting to panic.
Hasan: Why did you agree to twelve?
Fikri: [reflective] They needed an answer during the meeting. Everyone looked at me, and I wanted to be helpful.
Hasan: Wanting to help is good, but a promise should match your real ability.
Fikri: [desperate] I know. Should I stay awake for two nights and try to finish?
Hasan: [firmly] That may harm your work and the quality of the posters. Contact the organizer before the delay becomes a surprise.
Fikri: I feel embarrassed because they trusted me.
Hasan: [thoughtful] You can admit that your estimate was wrong and bring a solution, not only a problem.
Fikri: What solution would be fair?
Hasan: [practically] Offer four finished posters by Friday, simple templates for the remaining events, and a schedule for completing them next week.
Fikri: Could we also ask whether another volunteer can adapt the templates?
Hasan: [gently] Yes, if the organizer agrees. Give clear files and explain the fonts and sizes.
Fikri: I should not make a new promise before checking my calendar.
Hasan: [carefully] Exactly. Open it now and choose dates you can truly protect.
Fikri: I can finish four by Friday and four on each of the next two Tuesdays.
Hasan: [honestly] Then say that clearly and accept if they need a different arrangement.
Fikri: I will call this afternoon instead of sending a vague late-night message.
Hasan: [encouraging] Good. Keeping trust after a poor promise begins with early honesty and a realistic repair plan.

quiz.question: What did Fikri promise?
quiz.explanation: He accepted a large design task.

quiz.question: Why did he agree too quickly?
options: He felt pressure to be helpful in the meeting

quiz.question: Why does Hasan reject two sleepless nights?
options: They may harm work and poster quality
quiz.explanation: An unhealthy rescue plan creates more risk.

quiz.question: What immediate solution is suggested?
options: Four posters, templates, and a later schedule
quiz.explanation: The repair plan offers usable work and honest dates.

quiz.question: What should Fikri do before new promises?
options: Check and protect real calendar time
quiz.explanation: Reliable commitments begin with capacity checking.

quiz.question: What social pressure affected Fikri’s estimate?
options: Everyone expected an immediate helpful answer
quiz.explanation: Fikri agreed before checking actual capacity.

quiz.question: Why are two sleepless nights a poor repair?
options: They provide too much calendar time
They risk health, paid work, and poster quality
quiz.explanation: Fixing one promise should not create several new problems.

quiz.question: What makes Hasan’s proposal more than an excuse?
options: It asks the organizer to wait without details
It includes finished work, reusable templates, and dated follow-up
quiz.explanation: The alternative gives immediate value and a realistic path.

quiz.question: Why must the organizer agree before another volunteer adapts files?
options: The changed responsibility and method need consent
quiz.explanation: A repair plan cannot be imposed on the person depending on the promise.

quiz.question: What restores trust after the poor estimate?
options: Early honesty plus a schedule that matches real capacity
Staying silent until all work is done
quiz.explanation: Reliable repair begins before the delay becomes a surprise.
